```{r}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`misskappa` estimates weighted agreement coefficients (Conger, Fleiss,
Brennan–Prediger) when some ratings are **missing**, with standard errors,
confidence intervals, and equality tests.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(misskappa)
```

## A first agreement coefficient

`dat.gwet2014` is a small rating matrix (20 subjects, five raters, four
ordered categories) with some ratings missing (`NA`). The default estimator,
inverse-probability weighting (`"ipw"`), is consistent when ratings are
missing completely at random (MCAR) and is the recommended starting point:

```{r}
#| warning: false
fit <- agreement(dat.gwet2014, weight = "linear")
fit
```

Ratings can be numbers, strings, or factors. `categories = 0:4` would declare
a fifth, unused category, which changes Brennan–Prediger and the linear
weights. The print method shows each coefficient with its standard error and
a 95% confidence interval. The pieces are available directly:

```{r}
coef(fit)
sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))
```

### Confidence intervals

`confint()` gives natural-scale Wald intervals, or a variance-stabilizing
Fisher *z* interval that always stays inside `(-1, 1)`, useful when a
coefficient is close to the boundary:

```{r}
confint(fit)
confint(fit, transform = "fisher")
```

On complete data with few subjects, `confint(fit, method = "jackknife")` gives
exact delete-one jackknife intervals with a *t* critical value instead.
`?confint.misskappa_estimate` lists the fits that support it. For a tidy
summary, `as.data.frame(fit)` returns one row per coefficient with its
estimate, standard error, and interval.

## Choosing an estimator

Start with `"ipw"`. The others suit specific situations:

| Function and data | `estimator` | Assumption |
|---|---|---|
| `agreement()`, categorical ratings | `"ipw"` | MCAR, rater-varying observation rates |
| `agreement()`, categorical ratings | `"cat_fiml"` | Ignorable (MCAR or MAR), saturated multinomial |
| `agreement()`, scored ratings | `"pairwise"` | MCAR, distribution-free, saturated covariance |
| `agreement()`, scored ratings | `"nt_fiml"` | Ignorable, normal-theory, saturated covariance |
| `agreement()`, scored ratings | `"nt_fiml_cs"` | Ignorable, normal-theory, compound-symmetry covariance |
| `agreement_counts()`, category counts | `"fleiss_cuzick"` | MCAR, exchangeable raters |
| `agreement_counts()`, category counts | `"cat_fiml"` | Ignorable, exchangeable raters |
| `agreement_counts()`, category counts | `"nt_fiml_cs"` | Ignorable, exchangeable raters, normal-theory |

Use `"cat_fiml"` when missingness may depend on the observed ratings (MAR)
and there are few raters and categories. The scored estimators treat the
categories as numbers and use the quadratic weight. They report
Brennan–Prediger only when the scale is declared:

```{r}
agreement(dat.zapf2016, estimator = "pairwise")
agreement(dat.zapf2016, estimator = "nt_fiml", categories = 1:5)
```

`"nt_fiml_cs"` assumes compound symmetry, which lets it work on
planned-incomplete designs where some rater pairs never rate the same subject.
The [estimators article](articles/missingness-estimators.html) explains the
trade-offs and works through such a design.

## Counts-format data

When raters are interchangeable and you only have per-subject category counts,
use `agreement_counts()`. `dat.fleiss1971` is the classic psychiatric-diagnosis
table (30 subjects, six raters, five categories):

```{r}
agreement_counts(dat.fleiss1971)
```

`ratings_to_counts()` turns a subjects-by-raters matrix into this format.

## Beyond pairwise agreement

Set `g > 2` for kernels that compare `g` raters at once, or pass a
subjects-by-raters-by-features array for vector-valued ratings. The
[g-wise](articles/gwise-agreement.html) and
[vector-valued](articles/vector-valued-agreement.html) articles cover both.

## Testing whether coefficients are equal

`agreement_test()` tests whether a coefficient is the same across fits and
returns an `htest`. Fits are independent samples by default. Use
`paired = TRUE` for fits on the same subjects:

```{r}
agreement_test(AB = agreement(dat.zapf2016[, 1:2], estimator = "pairwise"),
               CD = agreement(dat.zapf2016[, 3:4], estimator = "pairwise"),
               paired = TRUE)
```

The [comparing coefficients](articles/equality-tests.html) article covers
one-sample, paired, and several-fit tests and custom contrasts.
